title: Critical Path Decomposition and KPI Cadence Notes
summary: Working doc that breaks a target feature rollout into its critical path, maps measurable KPIs to milestone cadence, and includes a compact capacity tally + go/no-go checklist for the launch week. Intended for daily standups in the two-week run-up and the 72h launch window. Drafted from product-ops + serving-runtime syncs; will be iterated with SRE and Solutions Eng before canary.
critical_path_milestones:
1) Feature freeze -> 2025-01-20 (owner: Marcus Chen) -- code merge, e2e tests green.
2) Staging performance signoff -> 2025-01-24 (owner: Tomás Rivera) -- p95 latency <= 240ms for 512 context baseline.
3) Dataset/Prompt regression sweep -> 2025-01-25 (owner: Evelyn Zhou) -- no more than 1% regression in quality metric per eval suite.
4) Canary config + routing policy ready -> 2025-01-27 (owner: Priya Singh) -- fallback model defined, routing rules in traffic router.
5) Operator runbook + alerting hooks -> 2025-01-28 (owner: Aisha Patel) -- runbook in Confluence, oncall notified.
6) Internal beta + pilot -> 2025-01-30 to 2025-02-02 (owner: Product PM) -- 1k users subset, monitor SLOs.
7) Full rollout window -> 2025-02-03 (owner: Product Ops) -- phased traffic increase per cadence below.
kpi_cadence_and_metrics:
Weekly cadence (pre-launch): product-ops sync + metrics review on Mondays. Daily cadence (T-7 to T+3): morning standup metric snapshot.
Primary KPIs to track (display on launch wall):
- Latency p50/p95 (ms) — target p95 <= 300ms during pilot, <= 400ms worst-case in surge.
- Error rate (5xx + application errors) — target < 0.5%, alert at >= 1%.
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD) — monitor delta vs baseline; alert if > +25%.
- Throughput (requests/sec) and avg batch size — track batching efficiency.
- Quality regressions — top-3 prompt suite failure rate; alert if > 1.5% degradations.
Metric windows and owners: nightly aggregation (SRE), morning snapshot + owner call (product-ops). Graphs: latency histogram, error heatmap by model/route, token-cost trend.
Escalation triggers: any sustained p95 > threshold for 10 minutes -> page SRE. Quality regression spike -> page applied-ml and product PM.
capacity_tally_estimates:
Quick capacity tally (T-7 baseline + surge):
- Baseline expected traffic: 120 requests/sec across hosted API routes.
- Pilot target traffic: +15% (burst to 140 req/s) for 24h windows.
- Greedy surge scenario (T+1 due to viral post): 250 req/s sustained for 3h.
GPU pool sizing notes: 1x g4dn-like pool handles ~40 req/s at 512 context with current model; recommended reserved pool during rollout = 6 nodes (headroom x1.5) -> target capacity ~240 req/s.
Autoscale policy: rapid scale to burst for 30m, then evaluate. Cache assumptions: prefix cache expected to reduce token count by ~18% in pilot cohort.
Cost sensitivity quick calc: at pilot throughput, expected incremental monthly cost = ~USD 7k (estimate), worst-case spike daily burn up to USD 1.2k/day while surge ongoing.

go_no_go_checklist:
Pre-rollout (T-0, 2 hours before incremental traffic):
- [ ] All CI checks green (Jenkins/Github Actions) (owner: Marcus)
- [ ] Staging p95 within threshold for 4h (owner: Tomás)
- [ ] Regression evals passed (owner: Evelyn)
- [ ] Canary routing + fallback tested (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Runbook published and paging verified (owner: Aisha)
Go criteria (must be all green): staging perf, quality, and operator readiness.
Abort criteria (any one): error rate spike > 1% sustained 10m, unknown data leakage detected, or capacity provisioning failure.
Rollback plan: immediate traffic switch to previous model variant, mark incident and create postmortem link (JIRA: PRODOPS-ROLLBACK-<date>), schedule root-cause within 24h.
open_questions_and_risks:
- How will third-party embeddings usage affect token cost during pilot? (owner: Finance)
- Risk: unexpected large user flows via a single route; mitigation: per-route throttles and quick traffic drain path.
- Risk: cross-region fallback latency; mitigation: pre-warm fallback pool in target region.
- Need final confirmation on KMS integration for private beta customers (security).
- Decision pending on conservative vs aggressive autoscale policy for first 48h; engineering to recommend by 2025-01-26.
